 \qquad \alpha\longmapsto[\alpha_*],$$ is bijective.
Let $\mathop{\mathrm{Isom}}_{\mathrm M}(V_K,V_L)$ be the set of $\Lambda$-linear isomorphisms $\Theta:V_K\to V_L$ satisfying $$(\Theta\otimes\Theta)(R_K)=R_L.$$

outputs.exact_statement:
Let $K/k$ and $L/l$ be finitely generated extensions of algebraically closed fields of characteristic $p$, with $$\mathop{\mathrm{trdeg}}(K/k)\ge2,\qquad \mathop{\mathrm{trdeg}}(L/l)\ge2.$$ The canonical map $$\mathop{\mathrm{Isom}}(K,k;L,l)\longrightarrow
 \mathop{\mathrm{Isom}}_{\mathrm M}(V_K,V_L)/\Lambda^\times,
 \qquad \alpha\longmapsto[\alpha_*],$$ is bijective.

Let $F$ be any field of characteristic $p$, and put $C=F^p$. If $C\subseteq M\subseteq F$ and $s\in F\setminus M$, then $[M(s):M]=p$. If $[F:C]$ is finite, every $p$-independent list extends to a $p$-basis $s_1,\ldots,s_e$ of $F/C$, with $[F:C]=p^e$ and monomial basis $$\{s_1^{i_1}\cdots s_e^{i_e}:0\leq i_j<p\}.$$ For such a basis there are commuting $C$-linear derivations $D_1,\ldots,D_e$ on $F$ satisfying $$D_j(s_1^{i_1}\cdots s_e^{i_e})
       =i_j s_1^{i_1}\cdots s_e^{i_e}.$$ On $C(s_j)$ the kernel of $D_j$ is $C$, and its nonzero eigenvectors with eigenvalue in $C$ are precisely the elements $c s_j^i$, where $c\in C^\times$ and $0\leq i<p$; their eigenvalues are $i\in\mathbf F_p$. Moreover, $C(s_j)\cap C(s_k)=C$ when $j\ne k$.

For $s,t\in F^\times$, one has $$s\notin C,\qquad \{s,t\}_F=0
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad t\in C(s).$$
Let $F$ have characteristic $p$, with $F\ne F^p$. If multiplication by $r\in\mathbf F_p^\times$ on $V_F$ maps every projective line over $F^p$ into a projective line, then $r=1$.

Let $K/k$ and $L/l$ be finitely generated extensions of algebraically closed fields of characteristic $p$, both of transcendence degree at least two. For every compatible isomorphism $\Theta:V_K\to V_L$, there is a unique $n\in\mathbf F_p^\times$ such that $\Psi=n\Theta$ sends every projective line over $K^p$ onto a projective line over $L^p$.

Let $E$ and $E'$ be finite-dimensional vector spaces over fields $H$ and $C$, respectively, with dimensions at least three. Every bijection $\psi:\mathbf P_H(E)\to\mathbf P_C(E')$ that maps lines onto lines is induced by an additive bijection $S:E\to E'$ satisfying $$S(av)=\sigma(a)S(v)\qquad(a\in H,\ v\in E)$$ for a field isomorphism $\sigma:H\to C$. The map $\sigma$ is unique, and $S$ is unique up to multiplication by an element of $C^\times$.
If $F/\kappa$ is a finitely generated extension of an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p$, then $$\bigcap_{m\ge1} F^{p^m}=\kappa.$$
